title: Seka Spear RDC Review - Mega Light Aero Bike?

takeaways.text: A size-L (standard geometry) RDC frame weighed 758 g; the Rapier cockpit is a required purchase in 19 width/stem combinations, and M/L also come in a lower, longer race geometry.

In the publication's independent rider-on wind-tunnel test it was the fastest all-rounder they had tested, 1.8 W faster than a Tarmac SL8, and it got slightly faster as yaw increased; changing wheels shifted the result by about 1.2 W.

On the road the cockpit felt wobbly in sprints and the frame flexed in hard corners, giving imprecise handling on twisty descents, but it was very comfortable on long rides compared with harsh aero bikes.
In their stiffness rig the bottom bracket was less stiff than the tester's steel road bike.
Frameset-only purchase priced about half an S-Works Tarmac frameset (about US$2,600 less) in July 2026; the tester would choose a standard Tarmac instead for $600 more.

disclosure: Published by Cyclingnews Tech. The description does not establish whether the test bike was supplied or whether the review was sponsored.
summary: Exact Spear RDC review presented with riding and wind-tunnel context. The test configuration is separate from this candidate's custom build; no aerodynamic ranking or specification is accepted from the video alone.
